def: Machine learning in which a model of many stacked layers learns its own features from data, trained by gradient descent.
A number that describes one aspect of an example, either designed by a person or learned by a model.
One adjustable step of a network that turns one description of an example into a new one.
An adjustable number inside a model, also called a weight, set during training.
A rule that turns how wrong a prediction was into a single number that training tries to reduce.
The algorithm that computes the gradient of the loss with respect to every parameter by applying the chain rule backwards through the network.
A neural network architecture, introduced in 2017, in which every position in a sequence attends directly to every other and all positions are processed in parallel.
A network that reads a sequence one element at a time and carries a hidden summary forward, which makes it inherently sequential.
A model that assigns a probability to what comes next in a sequence of text, given what came before.
A language model that predicts the next symbol from only the one symbol before it, using counted frequencies.
